mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW Z4 30i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW Z4 30i engine replacement typically costs £1,495-£3,800 supply-only for rebuilt units, or £2,800-£5,500 fitted by a specialist. Used M54B30 engines: £1,100-£1,600 supply-only. Used N52B30 engines: £1,200-£1,800 supply-only. Reconditioned N52B30 units: £2,000-£2,800 supply-only. Rebuilt M54B30 units: £2,200-£3,500 supply-only. Professional fitting adds £800-£1,500 depending on workshop location.

mainEntity.name: Which engine does the BMW Z4 30i have - M54 or N52?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Z4 30i badge spans two engine families depending on the generation: E85 Z4 3.0i (2003-2005): M54B30, 231hp, dual-VANOS. E85 Z4 3.0si (2006-2008): N52B30, 265hp, Valvetronic. E89 Z4 sDrive30i (2009-2016): N52B30, 258hp, Valvetronic. The N52 is BMW's final naturally aspirated straight-six - more powerful and efficient but with electric water pump and oil leak concerns.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW Z4 30i N52 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N52B30 is generally considered robust and 'pretty bulletproof' by owners, but it has known weaknesses: Electric water pump failure is common between 60k-80k miles - replace preventatively. Valve cover and oil filter housing gaskets leak as they age. Eccentric shaft sensor can fail, causing rough idle. Timing chain is durable - rarely fails before 180k miles. Regular oil changes with BMW LL-01 approved oil are essential.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of water pump failure in a BMW Z4 30i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N52's electric water pump can fail suddenly with little warning: Overheating within a mile of failure. No prior warning signs in many cases. Coolant loss without visible external leaks. Electric water pump failure is more common than mechanical pump failure on N52 engines. Proactive replacement at 60k-70k miles is strongly recommended.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a high-mileage BMW Z4 30i?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a Z4 30i worth £5,000-£15,000, a rebuilt engine at £2,200-£3,800 can make financial sense if the body, interior, and chassis are in good condition. Compare replacement cost against vehicle value - replacement is viable up to 70% of car's value. Early E85 3.0i and low-mileage E89 sDrive30i examples command higher values. Classic car values are rising - a well-maintained Z4 30i is a sound investment. Always factor 12-month warranty into replacement decision.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Z4 30i and the Z4 35i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The key differences between the Z4 30i and 35i are significant: 30i uses naturally aspirated N52B30, 255-265hp - simpler, more reliable. 35i uses turbocharged N54B30, 302hp - more power but HPFP and turbo failures common. 30i rebuilds are cheaper: £2,000-£2,800 vs £3,000+ for 35i. 30i avoids the turbo-related failures that plague the 35i. For long-term reliability, the 30i is often the better choice.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW Z4 30i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW Z4 30i badge spans two generations of the iconic roadster - the E85/E86 (2003-2008) and the E89 (2009-2016) - with two distinct 3.0-litre straight-six engines. The earlier M54B30 delivered 231hp with classic BMW inline-six character, while the later N52B30 introduced Valvetronic and magnesium-aluminium construction for 258hp and improved efficiency. Together, these engines represent the most popular naturally aspirated six-cylinder Z4s in the UK market.

milestones.description: E85 Z4 3.0i launched with M54B30, 231hp, 300Nm, dual-VANOS
E85 facelift: 3.0i replaced by 3.0si with N52B30, 265hp, Valvetronic
2008 - Z4 M (S54) and 3.0si (N52) produced alongside each other
E89 Z4 sDrive30i launched with N52B30, 258hp, 310Nm, retractable hardtop
End of E89 production; Z4 30i badge discontinued until G29 M40i
present - G29 Z4 M40i uses B58B30, but 30i badge not offered in the UK

commonProblems.h2: BMW Z4 30i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW Z4 30i's straight-six engines are among the most characterful powerplants BMW ever built, but age and mileage bring predictable issues. The M54B30 suffers from CCV and VANOS failures, while the N52B30 is plagued by electric water pump failures and oil leaks. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address these original failure points - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Electric Water Pump Failure - Why the BMW Z4 30i N52 Engine Overheats
problems.rootCause: The N52's electric water pump is a known weak point - when it fails, the engine overheats within a mile, often with no prior warning. The pump can fail suddenly, leaving the driver stranded and risking a warped cylinder head.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace electric water pump and thermostat, coolant flush
Supply & fit rebuilt N52B30 with new water pump, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if overheating caused head gasket or cylinder head damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW Z4 30i is worth £5,000-£15,000 depending on generation, mileage, and condition (`[THIRD-PARTY]` - Auto Trader market observation). Given the vehicle's enthusiast appeal and rising classic car values, engine replacement is generally viable for well-maintained examples. For higher-mileage examples with other wear issues, evaluate the vehicle's overall condition before committing.
problems.recommendation: On any N52-powered Z4 30i approaching 60,000 miles, proactive electric water pump replacement is the single best investment you can make. A £350-£550 specialist preventative replacement is far cheaper than a warped cylinder head or full engine replacement. As one owner noted: "The only preventative job some people often do is to replace the electric water pump, because when (not if) it dies the engine overheats within a mile."
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N52B30 engine prices for your BMW Z4 30i

problems.h4: CCV Failure - Why the BMW Z4 30i M54 Engine Burns Oil
problems.rootCause: The crankcase ventilation valve (CCV) diaphragm tears, allowing oil to be drawn into the intake manifold. Symptoms include excessive oil consumption (1L per 1,000 miles or more), blue smoke on start-up, and rough idle.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace CCV valve, all hoses, clean intake, oil change
repairOptions.longevity: Restores normal oil consumption; 60,000+ mile lifespan

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M54B30 with new CCV, valve stem seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil consumption has caused catalytic converter damage

problems.recommendation: CCV failure is one of the most common M54 issues and is relatively inexpensive to fix. At £300-£500 at a specialist, it's cheap insurance against catalytic converter damage. If you're seeing blue smoke on start-up but the car otherwise runs well, start with the CCV system before considering more expensive repairs.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for BMW Z4 30i M54 CCV repair and replacement

problems.h4: N52 Oil Leaks - Why the BMW Z4 30i Drips Oil
problems.rootCause: The N52's valve cover gasket and oil filter housing gasket become brittle with age and heat cycling, leading to oil leaks. If left unchecked, leaks can cause oil to drip onto the exhaust manifold, creating a burning smell and potential fire risk.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gasket and/or oil filter housing gasket
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; 50,000+ mile lifespan

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt N52B30 with new gaskets, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil starvation caused bearing damage

problems.recommendation: Oil leaks on the N52 are common but rarely catastrophic if addressed promptly. Check for oil around the valve cover and oil filter housing regularly. A £300-£550 specialist gasket replacement is cheap insurance against a more serious oil starvation issue.
problems.cta: -> Compare BMW Z4 30i N52 oil leak repair costs
